title: The tip rater
story:
Drivers have started rating customers, and the night manager wants it automated. Given how much a customer tipped and how late the delivery was, your script decides the rating, whether the delivery counts as late, whether the customer is owed a refund, and whether the driver earns a bonus.

The checker tries many tips and lateness values, including the exact edges of every rule, so read each boundary carefully.
create: Its first two lines declare `tip` and `minutesLate`, each in the form `local tip = 4` with a whole number.

requirements.text: It declares `tip` and `minutesLate` as `local name = wholeNumber`.
It runs without errors for every combination the checker tries.
It prints `Rating: Generous` for a tip of 10 or more, `Rating: Fair` for 3 to 9, `Rating: Stingy` for 1 or 2, and `Rating: None` for 0.
It prints `Late: yes` when `minutesLate` is more than 15, otherwise `Late: no`.
It prints `Refund: true` when the delivery was more than 30 minutes late, or more than 15 minutes late with no tip at all. Otherwise `Refund: false`.
It prints `Bonus: 5` when the tip is 10 or more and the delivery wasn't late at all (0 minutes), otherwise `Bonus: 0`. Work the bonus out with an if-expression.
It uses an `if` statement with at least one `elseif`.

hints: Do one line of output at a time. The rating is a chain of checks, from the biggest tip downwards.
The refund rule is two situations joined by or, and the second situation is itself two conditions joined by and. Brackets make it clear.
"More than 15" and "15 or more" are different. Check which operator each rule needs, then try the exact boundary numbers yourself.

static.fail: Create a Script named `TipRater` inside the `Test03` folder.
Work out the bonus with an if-expression, the kind that sits on the right of an equals sign.
Use an if statement with elseif for the rating.

check:
local path = "ServerScriptService.Course.Test03.TipRater"
local source = Course.source(path) or ""
local declared = true
for _, name in { "tip", "minutesLate" } do
	if not string.find(source, "local%s+" .. name .. "%s*=%s*%d+") then
		declared = false
		Course.fail("r2", "Couldn't find a line like `local " .. name .. " = 5` with a whole number. Write it exactly in that form.")
	end
end
if declared then
	Course.pass("r2")
end

local function has(prints, wanted)
	for _, line in prints do
		if line == wanted then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

local first = Course.run(path)
Course.check("r3", first.ok, "Your script stopped with an error: " .. tostring(first.error))

if not declared then
	for _, id in { "r4", "r5", "r6", "r7" } do
		Course.fail(id, "Not checked yet: the two starting lines need to be in the exact form shown, so the checker can try other numbers.")
	end
	return
end

local cases = { { 0, 0 }, { 1, 16 }, { 3, 15 }, { 9, 31 }, { 10, 0 }, { 10, 1 }, { 2, 20 }, { 0, 20 }, { 15, 45 }, { 0, 30 } }
for _, case in cases do
	local tip, late = case[1], case[2]
	local run = Course.run(path, { replace = {
		{ "local%s+tip%s*=%s*%d+", "local tip = " .. tip },
		{ "local%s+minutesLate%s*=%s*%d+", "local minutesLate = " .. late },
	} })
	local setup = string.format("With tip = %d and minutesLate = %d", tip, late)
	if not run.ok then
		Course.fail("r3", setup .. ", your script errored: " .. tostring(run.error))
	end
	local rating = if tip >= 10 then "Generous" elseif tip >= 3 then "Fair" elseif tip >= 1 then "Stingy" else "None"
	local lateText = if late > 15 then "yes" else "no"
	local refund = late > 30 or (late > 15 and tip == 0)
	local bonus = if tip >= 10 and late == 0 then 5 else 0
	local function expect(id, line)
		Course.check(id, has(run.prints, line), setup .. ", expected a line `" .. line .. "`. Your script printed " .. Course.show(run.prints))
	end
	expect("r4", "Rating: " .. rating)
	expect("r5", "Late: " .. lateText)
	expect("r6", "Refund: " .. tostring(refund))
	expect("r7", "Bonus: " .. bonus)
end
steps: Make the first two lines `local tip = 4` and `local minutesLate = 20`. You can pick any whole numbers.
Print the rating with an `if` / `elseif` chain: a tip of 10 or more prints `Rating: Generous`, 3 to 9 prints `Rating: Fair`, 1 or 2 prints `Rating: Stingy`, and 0 prints `Rating: None`.
Print `Late: yes` when minutesLate is more than 15 (so 16 and up), otherwise `Late: no`.
Print `Refund: true` when minutesLate is more than 30, or when minutesLate is more than 15 and the tip is exactly 0. Otherwise print `Refund: false`.

Print `Bonus: 5` when the tip is 10 or more and minutesLate is exactly 0, otherwise `Bonus: 0`. Work this one out with an if-expression, the one-line `if ... then ... else ...` that goes after an equals sign.
example:
With tip = 4 and minutesLate = 20:
Rating: Fair
Late: yes
Refund: false
Bonus: 0
